title: Error Handling (throw / catch)
lead: Xray uses a low-overhead value-return error channel: `throw <enum>` sets an error, `try/catch` handles it without PanicInfo allocation or stack unwinding.

sections.heading: throw
sections.markdown: `throw expr` writes an enum variant into the error channel and returns. The operand must be an enum variant value. No stack unwinding occurs.

sections.heading: try / catch
sections.markdown: `try { ... } catch (e: ErrType) { ... }` catches errors thrown within the try block. Typed catches filter by enum type; untyped `catch (e)` catches any error.

sections.heading: catch panic
sections.markdown: The panic channel is separate from ordinary enum errors. Each try has at most one panic handler: `catch panic { ... }`, `catch panic (p) { ... }`, or `catch panic (p: PanicInfo) { ... }`. An annotation must be exactly PanicInfo. The binding is read-only and scoped to its handler; copies preserve class identity and do not imply Sendable. A handler protects only its try body, so a panic raised in a handler seeks an outer handler. The language PanicInfo class includes message, code, stack, cause and data.

sections.heading: Error propagation
sections.markdown: Uncaught errors propagate up the call stack through the value-return channel. Each caller's `OP_ERR_CHECK` decides whether to enter a catch handler or continue propagating. `defer` blocks execute during propagation.

sections.heading: Debugger execution-flow boundaries
sections.markdown: Caught/uncaught debugger classification concerns the synchronous call chain of the current logical execution flow. A selected catch is caught; escape from the authenticated Instance or Task root is uncaught. A later await rethrow is classified in the awaiting flow. Observation precedes throw delivery and cleanup or handler effects. Registered generated-native code uses the current emitted protocol and owned registration. Resolved CALL primitives are copied after preparation, and actual child ENTER with exact binding/frame/thread proves admission before matching VM/native ancestors. Missing or old protocols reject before execution. Incomplete native origin coverage rejects all; incomplete handler routes reject caught/uncaught, preserving previous filters. All retains UNKNOWN for missing routes. Snapshots own native identity, Source coordinates and enum values without native locals or state, and continuation executes the original throw instruction once. Trusted canonical Source launch providers return same-proof native code, the current descriptor and a code lease, including native-only selections without unused VM entries. Receiving failures never fall back to VM; restart failure preserves the old stop, and detached execution retains its original code lease after adapter disposal. JSON stacks project authenticated Source coordinates without native locals or machine addresses. Native instruction breakpoints, startup pause with a native initializer or entry and native-only manual pause explicitly reject. Dynamic-library CLI loading, arbitrary native stepping and full safety qualification remain open.

sections.heading: defer must not let errors escape
sections.markdown: A `defer` is a cleanup edge, not an error-propagation edge (spec 8.3.1). The compiler rejects a deferred callable whose inferred error set is non-empty with `E0387`; absorb the error inside the body instead: `defer { try { close(c) } catch (e) { log.warn("close failed") } }`. An error or panic the body catches itself has not escaped. What static analysis cannot decide is backstopped at runtime: an error escaping a defer body terminates the process with `E0443`, exit status 70, uncatchable — it neither replaces nor suppresses an in-flight error. Go's "the defer's error wins" semantics were rejected because xray marks neither signatures nor call sites, so the substitution would be invisible in the source.

sections.heading: Design principles
bullets: Errors are values (enum variants), not exceptions
No PanicInfo allocation or stack unwinding; only a predictable branch at call boundaries that may propagate or catch errors
No `throws` in function signatures — errors are inferred, and `xray verify` freezes checked guarantees
Concrete error sets stay in the analyzer database; only a three-state throw-effect bit enters internal function types
Use ADT enums for structured error causes with exhaustive `match`
